messages:
incident-bot: P0 Pager — multiple GPU nodes reporting repeated OOM / CUDA driver resets, high 5xx rate for /v1/generate. Affects us-east serving pool. Paging oncall.
ash (oncall): I'm awake, looking. seeing huge scale up events in the autoscaler logs.
ash (oncall): quick summary: HPA/cluster-autoscaler tried to spin up 12 nodes, then nodes started flapping, kubelet reports `OOMKilled` and `nvidia: GPU reset` on multiple pods.
ben: any customer impact yet?
ash (oncall): yes, concern: queued requests and timeouts. Some customers hitting 502/504s and latency >10s. cust-success: getting DMs from a couple of enterprise customers saying inference is failing.
carla: logs? can you paste the pod crash reason?
ash (oncall): pasting stdout from a crashed runtime pod: ```
2026-03-15T02:12:07Z runtime: token gen start
[ERR] cuda: device-side assert triggered
runtime: kernel launch failed: out of memory
kubelet: container runtime: containerd: containerd: OOMKilled
```
eng-runtime: that cuda assert looks like GPU driver reset during allocation. when nodes add/evict GPUs can cause memory fragmentation and OOM during bootstrapping.
infra-bot: autoscaler events: `scale-up: from 3 -> 12` at 02:10; `node-notready` spikes at 02:11; `scale-down` triggered at 02:13 for 7 nodes. Rapid oscillation detected.
sre-lead: this is classic scale-thrash -> driver resets -> crashloops -> more unschedulable -> autoscaler panic. Need to break the loop.
ash (oncall): proposed immediate mitigations: 1) set autoscaler max to current (to stop new nodes) 2) cordon a few flapping nodes 3) patch runtime deployment to lower parallelism/replicas 4) switch to a safe model variant with lower mem footprint.
prod-ops: do we have a canary fallback model we can route to?
eng-runtime: yes, `gpt-lite-aug2025` is smaller and compatible. We can route 20% of traffic there as a slow ramp.
carla: do it. Nash, want me to take over routing?
nash (oncall): please. I'm going to throttle autoscaler now. running: ```kubectl patch hpa runtime-hpa -p '{"spec":{"maxReplicas":5}}'```
infra-bot: hpa patched to maxReplicas=5.
ash (oncall): cordoning two pending nodes: ```kubectl cordon gke-us-east-3-node-12``` and ```kubectl drain gke-us-east-3-node-9 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data```
infra-bot: node cordoned/drained. pods rescheduled.
ben: we're still seeing OOMKilled on some pods that got rescheduled to other nodes.
eng-runtime: try forcing a rolling restart of runtime pods to reset driver contexts: ```kubectl rollout restart deployment/runtime-service```. also reduce per-pod concurrency: patch deployment env `MAX_PARALLEL_REQUESTS=1`.
carla: applying rollout restart now.
prod-ops: routing 20% traffic to `gpt-lite-aug2025` via traffic-split. command: `kubectl apply -f traffic-split-lite.yaml`
prod-ops: traffic split applied.
cust-success: I told affected customers we're investigating and routing to a fallback; small % traffic may see different model.
sre-lead: keep autoscaler capped until we confirm node stability for 15m. Also add dampening: set cluster-autoscaler --scale-down-delay=10m and --expander=least-waste to reduce oscillation.
infra-bot: cluster-autoscaler args patched (scale-down-delay=10m).
ash (oncall): noticing driver kernel logs show `nvidia: GPU reset due to unknown error` coinciding with kubelet OOM signals. Could be a kernel module bug and stress from parallel init.
eng-runtime: we'll add a small init delay and remove aggressive pre-warming. patching DaemonSet to set `INIT_SLEEP=6` and reduce `CONCURRENT_WARMUPS` to 1.
carla: applying patch. logs show fewer GPU resets now.
ben: are we ok to start scaling slowly?
sre-lead: recommend manual scale up increments: set `maxReplicas=8`, `minReplicas=3`, then incremental if stable. Nash, you can nudge to 6 after 10m stable.
nash (oncall): set maxReplicas=8.
infra-bot: hpa patched to maxReplicas=8.
prod-ops: monitoring 5xx rate and P99 latency. 5xx rate dropping from 18% -> 6% after routing and restarts. P99 latency down to 2.1s.
cust-success: customers reporting partial recovery, one large customer still has intermittent 502s.
eng-runtime: investigating that customer's steady sessions — looks like long-lived KV cache causing memory bloat on their pods. we'll evict and rotate those pods.
carla: doing rolling restart for that subset via label `customer=large-x`.
nash (oncall): handing off to ben for the next shift, I've been oncall 2h. ben can you own the next 60m and call if anything regresses? :wave:
ben: taking it. I'll watch for crashloops and autoscaler events. leave notes pls.
ash (oncall): notes: 1) root cause interplay of rapid autoscale + GPU driver resets under parallel warmup -> OOMs 2) immediate mitigations: autoscaler cap, cordon/drain flapping nodes, reduce warmup concurrency, route to fallback model, rolling restarts 3) monitoring: 5xx and node-notready events 4) followups: collect dmesg from affected nodes and tag kernel/gpu driver team.
sre-lead: good handoff. ben, please coordinate with eng-runtime for a postmortem, timeline, and add action item to add autoscaler ramp control and safe warmup settings by default.
ben: will do. I'll also open an internal ticket and cc cust-success for follow-up comms.
prod-ops: closing incident page for now, keeping channel open for updates. :white_check_mark:
